subject: Future Tech
title: Quantum Simulation Power
description: A micro-lesson that makes Quantum Simulation Power usable.

hook.text: Simulating a caffeine molecule's electrons would overwhelm the best supercomputers. Quantum machines can handle it.

buildup.text: Quantum simulators map atoms onto qubits and let physics do the math instead of solving billions of equations.

discovery.text: Feynman predicted this: quantum systems are best simulated by other quantum systems obeying the same rules.

twist.text: Even noisy mid-size quantum machines already simulate small molecules more accurately than classical methods.

climax.text: Pharma and materials companies invest heavily, hoping quantum simulation will design better drugs and alloys.

punchline.text: Nature's math runs best on nature's hardware.

quiz.question: Why are quantum computers well suited to simulating molecules?
options: They follow the same quantum rules as atoms
